azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_api: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_api` is an API published within an Azure API Management workspace, scoped to and managed by that workspace's own decentralized team rather than the central platform team.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_api_l: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_api_link` associates an API within an API Management workspace with a shared API definition, letting a workspace publish an API owned elsewhere.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_api_v: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_api_version_set` groups related versioned API(s) together within an API Management workspace, so callers can navigate between version(s) of the same logical API.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_group: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_group` is a named collection of developer(s) within an API Management workspace, used to control which products they can access.
`azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_group_link` associates a group within an API Management workspace with a shared group definition.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_named: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_named_value` is a reusable configuration value (a secret or a plain string) within an API Management workspace, referenced by policy expressions scoped to that workspace.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_notif: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_notification` configures an email notification event (e.g. a new subscription request) for recipients within an API Management workspace.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_opera: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_operation` is a single documented HTTP operation (e.g. `GET /users`) belonging to an API within an API Management workspace.
`azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_operation_link` associates an operation within an API Management workspace with a shared operation definition.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_polic: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_policie` (a Policy) defines the request/response processing logic (rate limiting, transformation, authentication) applied to API traffic within an API Management workspace's own scope.
`azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_policy_fragment` is a reusable snippet of policy XML that can be included from multiple policy definitions within an API Management workspace.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_produ: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_product` bundles one or more API(s) together within an API Management workspace, the level subscription and access control are configured at.
`azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_product_link` associates a product within an API Management workspace with a shared product definition.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_relea: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_release` publishes a specific revision of an API within an API Management workspace live to developers.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_schem: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_schema` defines the data schema (JSON Schema, XML Schema) for request or response payloads on an API within an API Management workspace.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_subsc: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_subscription` grants a developer or app access to product(s) within an API Management workspace, carrying the subscription key(s) used to authenticate.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_tag: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_tag` is a label applied to API(s), operation(s), or product(s) within an API Management workspace, used for organization and discovery.
azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_works: `azure_apimanagement_apimworkspaces_workspace` is a self-contained administrative boundary within an API Management instance, letting a decentralized team own and manage its own API(s), product(s), and policy(ies) independently of the central platform team.
azure_app_openapi_auth_config: `azure_app_openapi_auth_config` configures authentication and authorization (identity provider(s), token validation) for a Container App.
azure_app_openapi_certificate: `azure_app_openapi_certificate` uploads a TLS certificate to a Container Apps environment, bindable to a custom domain.
azure_app_openapi_connected_environment: `azure_app_openapi_connected_environment` is a Container Apps environment running on Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes, for deploying container apps outside standard Azure regions.
azure_app_openapi_connected_environment_: `azure_app_openapi_connected_environment_storage` mounts an external storage volume accessible to container app(s) running in a Connected (Arc-enabled) Container Apps environment.
azure_app_openapi_container_app: `azure_app_openapi_container_app` is a Container App, a deployed, autoscaling container application running within a Container Apps environment.
azure_app_openapi_dapr_component: `azure_app_openapi_dapr_component` configures a Dapr building block (state store, pub/sub, secret store) made available to container app(s) in a Container Apps environment via the built-in Dapr sidecar.
azure_app_openapi_http_route_config: `azure_app_openapi_http_route_config` defines HTTP routing rule(s) directing matching traffic to a specific revision or target within a Container Apps environment.
azure_app_openapi_java_component: `azure_app_openapi_java_component` enables a managed Java runtime add-on (e.g. Config Server, Eureka service registry, Admin dashboard) for Java-based container app(s) in a Container Apps environment.
azure_app_openapi_job: `azure_app_openapi_job` runs a Container Apps container to completion for a batch, scheduled, or event-driven task, rather than serving ongoing request traffic like a Container App.
azure_app_openapi_maintenance_configurat: `azure_app_openapi_maintenance_configuration_resource` defines a preferred maintenance window for platform updates to a Container Apps environment.
azure_app_openapi_managed_certificate: `azure_app_openapi_managed_certificate` is an automatically provisioned and renewed free TLS certificate for a custom domain bound to a Container App.
azure_app_openapi_managed_environment: `azure_app_openapi_managed_environment` is the Container Apps environment -- the secure, isolated boundary sharing a virtual network and Log Analytics workspace -- that container app(s) and job(s) are deployed within.
azure_app_openapi_managed_environment_st: `azure_app_openapi_managed_environment_storage` mounts an external storage volume (Azure Files) accessible to container app(s) running in a Container Apps environment.
azure_app_openapi_private_endpoint_conne: `azure_app_openapi_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and a Container Apps environment, tracking its own approval state.
azure_app_openapi_session_pool: `azure_app_openapi_session_pool` provisions a pool of prewarmed, isolated Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions, used for secure, fast-starting per-session code execution (e.g. an AI agent's own code interpreter).
azure_app_openapi_source_control: `azure_app_openapi_source_control` configures continuous deployment for a Container App from a linked source control repository.
azure_app_openapi_workflow_envelope: `azure_app_openapi_workflow_envelope` describes a single Logic Apps (Standard) workflow hosted within a Container Apps-based Logic App resource.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_api_portal: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_api_portal_custom_domain_resource` maps a custom domain to an Azure Spring Apps API portal, the self-service API documentation and testing UI for services in the app.
`azure_appplatform_appplatform_api_portal_resource` deploys the API portal, a self-service UI aggregating OpenAPI documentation for every service registered in an Azure Spring Apps app.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_apm_resour: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_apm_resource` configures an Application Performance Monitoring integration (e.g. Application Insights, Dynatrace) for services running in an Azure Spring Apps instance.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_app_resour: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_app_resource` is a single microservice application deployed within an Azure Spring Apps service instance, that deployment(s) and binding(s) belong to.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_applicatio: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_application_accelerator_resource` enables Application Accelerator, generating new Spring Boot project scaffolding from predefined or customized templates within Azure Spring Apps.

`azure_appplatform_appplatform_application_live_view_resource` enables Application Live View, an embedded Spring Boot Actuator-based dashboard for inspecting running app health and metrics in Azure Spring Apps.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_binding_re: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_binding_resource` connects an Azure Spring Apps application to a backing service (a database, a message broker) by injecting its own connection details as environment configuration.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_build: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_build` is a single build execution compiling application source code into a deployable container image within Azure Spring Apps' own build service.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_build_serv: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_build_service` is the Cloud Native Buildpacks-based build service within an Azure Spring Apps instance that compiles source code into container images.
`azure_appplatform_appplatform_build_service_agent_pool_resource` provisions compute capacity dedicated to running Azure Spring Apps build service jobs.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_builder_re: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_builder_resource` defines the buildpack(s) and stack used by Azure Spring Apps' own build service to compile application source into a container image.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_buildpack_: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_buildpack_binding_resource` supplies configuration or credentials (e.g. an APM key) that a specific buildpack needs at build time within Azure Spring Apps.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_certificat: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_certificate_resource` uploads a TLS certificate to Azure Spring Apps, bindable to a custom domain.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_configurat: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_configuration_service_resource` provisions Application Configuration Service, which centrally serves externalized configuration (from a linked Git repository) to applications running in Azure Spring Apps.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_container_: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_container_registry_resource` registers a container registry (in addition to the default one) that Azure Spring Apps can pull custom container image deployments from.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_custom_dom: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_custom_domain_resource` maps a custom domain to a specific application within an Azure Spring Apps instance.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_customized: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_customized_accelerator_resource` registers a caller-authored project template for Azure Spring Apps' own Application Accelerator, beyond the built-in template set.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_deployment: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_deployment_resource` is a specific, running deployment of an Azure Spring Apps application's own code, the unit compute resources and instance count are configured on.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_dev_tool_p: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_dev_tool_portal_resource` deploys the Dev Tool Portal, a unified UI aggregating Application Accelerator, API portal, and other developer tooling for an Azure Spring Apps instance.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_gateway_cu: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_gateway_custom_domain_resource` maps a custom domain to the Spring Cloud Gateway front door of an Azure Spring Apps instance.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_gateway_re: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_gateway_resource` deploys Spring Cloud Gateway, the managed API gateway routing external traffic to application(s) within an Azure Spring Apps instance.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_gateway_ro: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_gateway_route_config_resource` defines routing rule(s) directing matching Spring Cloud Gateway traffic to a specific application within Azure Spring Apps.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_service_re: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_service_registry_resource` provisions a Spring Cloud service registry (Eureka-compatible) within Azure Spring Apps, letting applications discover each other by logical name.

`azure_appplatform_appplatform_service_resource` is the top-level Azure Spring Apps service instance that application(s) and their own shared infrastructure (gateway, config service, registry) are deployed within.
azure_appplatform_appplatform_storage_re: `azure_appplatform_appplatform_storage_resource` mounts an external storage account (e.g. Azure Files) as a persistent volume accessible to applications running in Azure Spring Apps.
azure_automation_openapi_automation_acco: `azure_automation_openapi_automation_account` is the top-level Azure Automation resource that runbook(s), schedule(s), and other automation asset(s) are organized within.
azure_automation_openapi_certificate: `azure_automation_openapi_certificate` stores a certificate securely within an Azure Automation account, referenced by runbook(s) needing it for authentication.
azure_automation_openapi_connection: `azure_automation_openapi_connection` stores connection details for an external service (of a specific connection type) that Azure Automation runbook(s) authenticate against.
azure_automation_openapi_connection_type: `azure_automation_openapi_connection_type` defines the schema (field names) for a category of Azure Automation connection, e.g. the fields needed to connect to Azure itself.
azure_automation_openapi_credential: `azure_automation_openapi_credential` stores a username/password credential securely within an Azure Automation account, referenced by runbook(s).
azure_automation_openapi_dsc_configurati: `azure_automation_openapi_dsc_configuration` defines a PowerShell Desired State Configuration script managed by Azure Automation State Configuration, describing the target state for registered node(s).
azure_automation_openapi_dsc_node_config: `azure_automation_openapi_dsc_node_configuration` is a compiled DSC configuration assigned to specific registered node(s), the actual configuration those nodes are enforced against.
azure_automation_openapi_hybrid_runbook_: `azure_automation_openapi_hybrid_runbook_worker` registers a machine (on-premises or another cloud) as a hybrid worker, letting Azure Automation runbooks execute directly on it rather than Azure-hosted sandboxes.
`azure_automation_openapi_hybrid_runbook_worker_group` groups related hybrid runbook worker(s) together, that a runbook job can be targeted to run on any member of.
azure_automation_openapi_job: `azure_automation_openapi_job` is a single execution of an Azure Automation runbook.
azure_automation_openapi_job_schedule: `azure_automation_openapi_job_schedule` links an Azure Automation runbook to a schedule, triggering it to run automatically at the schedule's own defined times.
azure_automation_openapi_module: `azure_automation_openapi_module` imports a PowerShell module into an Azure Automation account, making its own cmdlets available to runbook(s).
azure_automation_openapi_package: `azure_automation_openapi_package` imports a Python package into an Azure Automation account, making it available to Python runbook(s).
azure_automation_openapi_private_endpoin: `azure_automation_openapi_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an Azure Automation account, tracking its own approval state.
azure_automation_openapi_runbook: `azure_automation_openapi_runbook` is the executable script (PowerShell, Python, or a graphical workflow) that Azure Automation runs, either on a schedule, on demand, or via webhook.
azure_automation_openapi_runtime_environ: `azure_automation_openapi_runtime_environment` defines a custom language version and package set that PowerShell or Python runbook(s) execute within, beyond Azure Automation's own default runtime.
azure_automation_openapi_schedule: `azure_automation_openapi_schedule` defines a recurring or one-time trigger time that Azure Automation runbook(s) can be linked to for automatic execution.
azure_automation_openapi_software_update: `azure_automation_openapi_software_update_configuration` schedules Azure Automation Update Management to deploy OS patches across a defined set of machine(s) on a recurring maintenance window.
azure_automation_openapi_source_control: `azure_automation_openapi_source_control` links an Azure Automation account to an external Git repository, syncing runbook source code automatically on push.
azure_automation_openapi_variable: `azure_automation_openapi_variable` stores a named configuration value (plain or encrypted) within an Azure Automation account, referenced by runbook(s).
azure_automation_openapi_watcher: `azure_automation_openapi_watcher` runs a long-lived Azure Automation script that watches for a defined condition and triggers a follow-up runbook when it's detected.
azure_automation_openapi_webhook: `azure_automation_openapi_webhook` exposes an HTTP endpoint that, when called, triggers a specific Azure Automation runbook to run.
azure_availability_set: `azure_availability_set` groups VMs so a single hardware failure or maintenance event can't take down every instance of an application at once. Azure spreads the VMs across up to 3 fault domains (shared power and network switch) and up to 20 update domains (VMs that restart together during planned maintenance), and neither count can change after the set is created. There's no extra cost for using one, but Microsoft's own current guidance recommends Virtual Machine Scale Sets with flexible orchestration for new deployments needing the widest range of availability features.
azure_capacity_reservation: `azure_capacity_reservation` reserves compute capacity for one specific VM size in one region or zone, for as long as you keep it. Unlike a Reserved Instance, there's no one- or three-year term: you create and delete a reservation whenever you want, and it's billed at the same pay-as-you-go rate as the VM size itself whether a VM is actually using it or not. A VM only consumes the reservation if it explicitly specifies it in its own properties.
azure_capacity_reservation_group: `azure_capacity_reservation_group` is the parent resource every individual capacity reservation belongs to. It pins the region (and, optionally, which availability zones are eligible) for every reservation created inside it, and it's what a VM's own properties reference to actually consume a reservation -- a group can hold at most one reservation per VM size per zone.
azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservice: `azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_account` provisions an Azure AI services (Cognitive Services) account -- or an Azure AI Foundry (Microsoft Foundry) resource -- the top-level container that model deployment(s) and API access are billed and managed under.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_agent_application` registers an AI agent application built on Azure AI Foundry's own Agent Service, the deployable unit an agent's tools and instructions are packaged into.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_agent_deployment` is a specific, running deployment of an Azure AI Foundry agent application, servable for real conversation traffic.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_capability_host` provisions the compute and storage backing a specific AI capability (e.g. agent execution) within an Azure AI Foundry account.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_commitment_plan` purchases a fixed monthly commitment tier for an Azure AI services feature (e.g. Translator or Speech), at a discount versus pay-as-you-go pricing.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_commitment_plan_account_association` attaches an Azure AI services account to a commitment plan, applying the plan's own discounted pricing to that account's usage.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_connection_properties_v2_basic_resource` defines a connection from an Azure AI Foundry account to an external resource (a data source, an API key-authenticated service).

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_defender_for_aisetting` enables Microsoft Defender for AI protection on an Azure AI services account, surfacing threat alerts for anomalous or malicious AI workload activity in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_deployment` is a specific model deployment (e.g. a GPT or embedding model) on an Azure AI services / Azure OpenAI account, servable for inference calls.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_encryption_scope` defines a customer-managed encryption key configuration scoped to a subset of data within an Azure AI services account.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_managed_network_settings_properties_basic_resource` configures whether an Azure AI Foundry account's own managed virtual network allows all outbound traffic by default or only explicitly approved outbound rule(s).

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_network_security_perimeter_configuration` associates an Azure AI services account with a network security perimeter, restricting its own network access to the perimeter's own boundary rules.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_outbound_rule_basic_resource` defines an allowed outbound network destination for an Azure AI Foundry account's own managed virtual network, permitting egress to a specific service.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an Azure AI services account, tracking its own approval state.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_project` is a project within an Azure AI Foundry account, scoping model deployment(s), agent(s), and connection(s) to a specific team or workload.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_project_capability_host` provisions the compute and storage backing a specific AI capability (e.g. agent execution) scoped to a single Azure AI Foundry project, rather than the whole account.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_quota_tier` reports the throughput quota tier assigned to a specific model within an Azure AI services account, e.g. tokens-per-minute limits.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_rai_blocklist` defines a custom list of blocked term(s) or phrase(s) enforced by a Responsible AI content filter policy on Azure AI services model deployment(s).
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_rai_blocklist_item` is a single blocked term or phrase within a Responsible AI blocklist.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_rai_external_safety_provider_schema` integrates a third-party content-safety guardrail provider (e.g. Palo Alto Networks) into an Azure AI Foundry Responsible AI policy, alongside Microsoft's own built-in filters.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_rai_policy` defines the Responsible AI content filter configuration (categories, severity thresholds) enforced on Azure AI services model deployment(s) it's attached to.

`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_rai_tool_label` classifies a specific tool an AI agent can call under a Responsible AI risk category, so Foundry Guardrails can apply appropriate policy when that tool is invoked.
`azure_cognitiveservices_cognitiveservices_rai_topic` defines a custom sensitive topic a Responsible AI content filter policy detects and restricts, beyond Microsoft's own built-in harm categories.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_keyspa: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_keyspace_get_results` is a Cassandra API keyspace within a Cosmos DB account, the container tables in that API surface are organized under.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_a: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_assignment_resource` grants a Cassandra API role definition's own permissions to a specific identity within a Cosmos DB account.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_d: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_definition_resource` defines a set of data-plane permissions that can be granted to identities accessing a Cosmos DB account through its Cassandra API.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_table_: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_table_get_results` is a table within a Cosmos DB account's Cassandra API keyspace.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_client_encryptio: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_client_encryption_key_get_results` is a client-side encryption key registered with a Cosmos DB database, used to encrypt specific field(s) before they're sent to the service.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cluster_resource: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cluster_resource` provisions an Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra cluster, a fully managed deployment of open-source Cassandra.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_data_center_reso: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_data_center_resource` is a single data center (a group of nodes in one region) within an Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra cluster.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_database_account: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_database_account_get_results` is a Cosmos DB account, the top-level resource that database(s) across any of its enabled API surfaces (SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table) are created within.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleet_resource: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleet_resource` is a Cosmos DB Fleet, a top-level resource organizing and managing multiple Cosmos DB account(s) -- typically one per tenant -- across subscriptions and resource groups for a single multitenant application.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_accou: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_account_resource` associates a specific Cosmos DB account with a fleetspace, making it part of that fleetspace's own shared throughput pool.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_resou: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_resource` is a logical grouping of Cosmos DB account(s) within a fleet, optionally sharing a pooled throughput allocation across every account in the group.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_database: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_database_get_results` is a database within a Cosmos DB account's Gremlin (graph) API surface, the container graph(s) are organized under.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_graph_ge: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_graph_get_results` is a graph within a Cosmos DB account's Gremlin API database, storing vertex and edge data queried via the Gremlin traversal language.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_role_ass: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_role_assignment_resource` grants a Gremlin API role definition's own permissions to a specific identity within a Cosmos DB account.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_role_def: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_role_definition_resource` defines a set of data-plane permissions that can be granted to identities accessing a Cosmos DB account through its Gremlin API.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_dbcollecti: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_dbcollection_get_results` is a collection within a Cosmos DB account's MongoDB API database.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_dbdatabase: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_dbdatabase_get_results` is a database within a Cosmos DB account's MongoDB API surface, the container collection(s) are organized under.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_mirole_ass: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_mirole_assignment_resource` grants a MongoDB role definition's own permissions to a specific identity on a Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore/MI) instance.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_mirole_def: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_mirole_definition_resource` defines a set of data-plane permissions that can be granted to identities accessing a Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore/MI) instance.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_role_defin: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_role_definition_get_results` defines a set of data-plane permissions that can be granted to identities accessing a Cosmos DB account through its MongoDB API.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_user_defin: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_mongo_user_definition_get_results` defines a MongoDB API user on a Cosmos DB account, with its own assigned role(s) for data-plane access.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_notebook_workspa: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_notebook_workspace` provisions a hosted Jupyter notebook environment attached to a Cosmos DB account, for interactively exploring and analyzing its own data.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_private_endpoint: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and a Cosmos DB account, tracking its own approval state.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_service_resource: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_service_resource` enables and configures an optional Cosmos DB add-on capability (e.g. a dedicated gateway or materialized views builder) on an account.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_container_ge: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_container_get_results` is a container within a Cosmos DB account's SQL (NoSQL) API database, storing item(s) with its own partition key and indexing policy.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_database_get: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_database_get_results` is a database within a Cosmos DB account's SQL (NoSQL) API surface, the container container(s) are organized under.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_role_assignm: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_role_assignment_get_results` grants a SQL API role definition's own permissions to a specific identity within a Cosmos DB account.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_role_definit: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_role_definition_get_results` defines a set of data-plane permissions that can be granted to identities accessing a Cosmos DB account through its SQL (NoSQL) API.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_stored_proce: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_stored_procedure_get_results` is a JavaScript stored procedure registered on a Cosmos DB SQL API container, executed server-side against its own data.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_trigger_get_: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_trigger_get_results` is a JavaScript trigger registered on a Cosmos DB SQL API container, running automatically before or after a specific data operation.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_user_defined: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_sql_user_defined_function_get_results` is a JavaScript user-defined function registered on a Cosmos DB SQL API container, callable from within queries.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_table_get_result: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_table_get_results` is a table within a Cosmos DB account's Table API surface.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_table_role_assig: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_table_role_assignment_resource` grants a Table API role definition's own permissions to a specific identity within a Cosmos DB account.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_table_role_defin: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_table_role_definition_resource` defines a set of data-plane permissions that can be granted to identities accessing a Cosmos DB account through its Table API.
azure_dedicated_host: `azure_dedicated_host` maps to one physical server in an Azure datacenter, allocated entirely to your own subscription -- no other customer's VMs are ever placed on it. Beyond the isolation itself, a dedicated host gives you Azure Hybrid Benefit licensing, control over when platform maintenance actually lands on your hardware, and a say in which of your own workloads share the same physical memory and storage. Each host is created inside a host group and can run multiple VMs at once, as long as they're all from the same size series.
azure_dedicated_host_group: `azure_dedicated_host_group` is the resource that represents a collection of dedicated hosts. It's created in a specific region and, if you want zone-level fault isolation, a specific availability zone -- every host you add to the group inherits that placement. The group also controls whether new VMs get placed onto its hosts automatically or only when you explicitly pick a host.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_ca_certificate: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_ca_certificate` registers a CA certificate an Event Grid namespace trusts for validating client certificates during MQTT mutual TLS authentication.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_channel: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_channel` establishes the event delivery link between an Event Grid partner topic (or partner destination) and the consuming or publishing Azure subscription.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_client: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_client` registers an MQTT client identity permitted to connect to an Event Grid namespace's own MQTT broker.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_client_group: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_client_group` groups related Event Grid MQTT client(s) together by a matching expression, so permission bindings and topic spaces can target the group instead of individual clients.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_domain: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_domain` is a management tier grouping many related Event Grid topics together under a single endpoint and access control boundary, for large-scale multi-tenant event publishing scenarios.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_domain_topic: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_domain_topic` is a single logical topic within an Event Grid domain, that event subscription(s) are created against.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_event_subscrip: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_event_subscription` subscribes a destination (a webhook, Azure Function, or queue) to matching event(s) published on an Event Grid topic or Azure resource.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_namespace: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_namespace` is an Event Grid namespace, the newer resource providing both MQTT broker capability and namespace topics for pull or push event delivery.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_namespace_topi: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_namespace_topic` is a topic within an Event Grid namespace, that publisher(s) send CloudEvents-formatted event(s) into and event subscription(s) pull or receive push delivery from.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_partner_namesp: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_partner_namespace` is the resource a registered Event Grid partner publishes third-party SaaS event(s) into, for delivery to subscribed Azure customer(s).
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_partner_regist: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_partner_registration` registers a third-party SaaS provider as an Event Grid partner, authorizing it to publish events into customer Azure subscriptions.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_partner_topic: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_partner_topic` is the customer-side topic receiving event(s) published by a registered Event Grid partner's own SaaS platform.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_permission_bin: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_permission_binding` grants an Event Grid MQTT client or client group publish or subscribe permission on a specific topic space.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_private_endpoi: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an Event Grid topic, domain, or namespace, tracking its own approval state.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_subscription: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_subscription` subscribes a destination to matching event(s) published on an Event Grid topic or Azure resource.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_system_topic: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_system_topic` is the built-in Event Grid topic automatically available for a specific Azure resource (e.g. a Storage account) to publish its own lifecycle event(s) from.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_topic: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_topic` is a custom Event Grid topic, the endpoint a caller-defined application publishes its own event(s) to.
azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_topic_space: `azure_eventgrid_eventgrid_topic_space` is a named group of MQTT topic pattern(s) within an Event Grid namespace, that permission binding(s) grant client access to collectively.
azure_image: `azure_image` defines a reusable, versioned VM image inside an Azure Compute Gallery, built from an existing VM, a VHD, a snapshot, a managed image, or another image version. An image definition describes what the image is (Windows or Linux, generalized or specialized, memory requirements); an image version is the actual buildable artifact you point a new VM at, and you can keep several versions of the same definition side by side, replicated to whichever regions you choose.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_ba: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_batch_deployment` is a specific model deployment behind an Azure Machine Learning batch endpoint, processing large offline datasets asynchronously rather than serving real-time requests.
`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_batch_endpoint` is the stable, addressable endpoint that Azure Machine Learning batch deployment(s) are invoked through for offline, large-scale scoring jobs.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_ca: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_capability_host` provisions the compute and storage backing a specific AI capability (e.g. agent execution, RAG indexing) within an Azure AI Foundry hub or project.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_co: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_code_container` is the named container in an Azure Machine Learning workspace that version(s) of a specific piece of source code are registered under.

`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_code_version` is a specific, immutable version of source code registered in an Azure Machine Learning workspace, referenced by job(s) and component(s) that use it.
`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_component_container` is the named container in an Azure Machine Learning workspace that version(s) of a reusable pipeline component are registered under.
`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_component_version` is a specific, immutable version of a reusable Azure Machine Learning pipeline component.

`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_compute_resource` provisions compute (a compute instance, cluster, or attached external compute) within an Azure Machine Learning workspace, that training and inference workload(s) run on.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_da: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_data_container` is the named container in an Azure Machine Learning workspace that version(s) of a registered dataset are grouped under.
`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_data_version_base` is a specific, immutable version of a dataset registered in an Azure Machine Learning workspace.

`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_datastore` registers a connection to an external storage account (Blob, Data Lake, or similar) with an Azure Machine Learning workspace, that dataset(s) are sourced from.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_en: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_environment_container` is the named container in an Azure Machine Learning workspace that version(s) of a training/inference environment definition are registered under.

`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_environment_version` is a specific, immutable version of a training or inference software environment (a container image or Conda spec) registered in an Azure Machine Learning workspace.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_fe: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_featureset_container` is the named container in an Azure Machine Learning workspace that version(s) of a feature set are registered under, part of the Managed Feature Store capability.
`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_featureset_version` is a specific, immutable version of a feature set definition in an Azure Machine Learning Managed Feature Store.

`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_featurestore_entity_container` is the named container in an Azure Machine Learning workspace that version(s) of a feature store entity (e.g. `customer`) are registered under.
`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_featurestore_entity_version` is a specific, immutable version of a feature store entity definition, specifying its own join key(s).
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_jo: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_job_base` is an Azure Machine Learning job -- a training run, pipeline execution, or sweep -- submitted to run on workspace compute.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_ma: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_marketplace_subscription` subscribes an Azure Machine Learning workspace to a model or offer available through the Azure Marketplace, required before deploying certain third-party Model Catalog models.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_mo: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_model_container` is the named container in an Azure Machine Learning workspace that version(s) of a registered model are grouped under.
`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_model_version` is a specific, immutable version of a model registered in an Azure Machine Learning workspace, deployable to an online or batch endpoint.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_on: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_online_deployment` is a specific model deployment behind an Azure Machine Learning online endpoint, serving real-time inference requests.

`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_online_endpoint` is the stable, addressable endpoint that Azure Machine Learning online deployment(s) are invoked through for real-time inference, with traffic splitting across them.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_ou: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_outbound_rule_basic_resource` defines an allowed outbound network destination for an Azure Machine Learning workspace's own managed virtual network, permitting egress to a specific service.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_pr: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an Azure Machine Learning workspace, tracking its own approval state.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_re: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_registry` is an Azure Machine Learning registry, a shared catalog letting model(s), environment(s), and component(s) be published and consumed across multiple workspaces and regions.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_sc: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_schedule` triggers an Azure Machine Learning job or pipeline to run automatically on a recurring cron-style schedule.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_se: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_serverless_endpoint` deploys a Models as a Service (MaaS) foundation model from the Azure AI Foundry Model Catalog to a pay-per-token serverless endpoint, without provisioning dedicated compute.
azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_wo: `azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_workspace` is the top-level Azure Machine Learning (or Azure AI Foundry hub) resource that compute, datastore(s), and every registered asset are organized within.

`azure_machinelearningservices_openapi_workspace_connection_properties_v2_basic_resource` defines a connection from an Azure Machine Learning workspace to an external resource (a data source, an API key-authenticated service) that jobs and components can reference.
azure_network_networkmanager_admin_rule_: `azure_network_networkmanager_admin_rule_collection` groups related security admin rule(s) together within an Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin configuration.
azure_network_networkmanager_base_admin_: `azure_network_networkmanager_base_admin_rule` is the base type for a security admin or default rule enforced centrally across a Virtual Network Manager network group, evaluated before any local NSG rules.
azure_network_networkmanager_commit: `azure_network_networkmanager_commit` deploys a Virtual Network Manager configuration (connectivity or security) to its own target scope, making it take actual effect.
azure_network_networkmanager_connectivit: `azure_network_networkmanager_connectivity_configuration` defines the connectivity topology (hub-and-spoke or mesh) Azure Virtual Network Manager establishes across the virtual network(s) in a network group.
azure_network_networkmanager_network_gro: `azure_network_networkmanager_network_group` is a named collection of virtual network(s), defined statically or dynamically via Azure Policy conditions, that Virtual Network Manager configurations are applied to.
azure_network_networkmanager_network_man: `azure_network_networkmanager_network_manager` is the top-level Azure Virtual Network Manager resource, centrally managing connectivity and security configuration across virtual network(s) within its own scope.
`azure_network_networkmanager_network_manager_connection` delegates management of a subscription or management group's own virtual networks to a Virtual Network Manager instance in a different scope.
`azure_network_networkmanager_network_manager_routing_configuration` defines centralized routing rule(s) Virtual Network Manager applies across the virtual network(s) in a network group.
azure_network_networkmanager_routing_rul: `azure_network_networkmanager_routing_rule` is a single centrally managed route within a Virtual Network Manager routing configuration.
`azure_network_networkmanager_routing_rule_collection` groups related centrally managed routing rule(s) together within a Virtual Network Manager routing configuration.
azure_network_networkmanager_scope_conne: `azure_network_networkmanager_scope_connection` extends a Virtual Network Manager instance's own management scope to include another subscription or management group.
azure_network_networkmanager_security_ad: `azure_network_networkmanager_security_admin_configuration` defines centrally enforced security admin rule(s) that Virtual Network Manager applies across the virtual network(s) in a network group, taking precedence over local NSG rules.
azure_network_networkmanager_security_us: `azure_network_networkmanager_security_user_configuration` defines security user rule(s) Virtual Network Manager applies across the virtual network(s) in a network group, evaluated after local NSG rules.
`azure_network_networkmanager_security_user_rule` is a single centrally managed security rule within a Virtual Network Manager security user configuration.
`azure_network_networkmanager_security_user_rule_collection` groups related security user rule(s) together within a Virtual Network Manager security user configuration.
azure_network_networkmanager_static_memb: `azure_network_networkmanager_static_member` explicitly adds a specific virtual network to a Virtual Network Manager network group, as an alternative to dynamic, Azure Policy-based group membership.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_address_pre: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_address_prefix_set` defines a named, reusable set of IP address prefixes managed by Azure Virtual Network Manager, referenced by IP address management pools and connectivity/security configurations.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_application: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_application_security_group` groups network interface(s) together as a named, logical unit, letting network security group rules reference the group instead of raw IP addresses.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_bastion_hos: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_bastion_host` provisions Azure Bastion, a managed jump host providing secure RDP/SSH access to VMs over the Azure portal without exposing them to public IP addresses.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_custom_ip_p: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_custom_ip_prefix` brings a caller-owned public IP address range into Azure for advertisement and use, via Custom IP Prefix (BYOIP).
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_custom: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_custom_policy` overrides Azure DDoS Protection's own default traffic thresholds for a specific public IP address, tuning detection sensitivity for that resource's own traffic pattern.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_protec: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_protection_plan` subscribes one or more virtual networks to Azure DDoS Network Protection, providing enhanced mitigation, telemetry, and cost protection beyond the free basic tier.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_dscp_config: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_dscp_configuration` marks matching outbound traffic from a network interface with a specific DSCP value, for downstream Quality of Service traffic prioritization.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_inbound_sec: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_inbound_security_rule` allows specific inbound traffic through an Azure Firewall-integrated security partner provider before it reaches a virtual network.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_allocati: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_allocation` reserves a specific IP address block for a defined purpose (e.g. an Azure PaaS service delegation) within a virtual network's own address space.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_group: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_group` is a named, reusable collection of IP address(es) or address range(s) that Azure Firewall rules can reference by name instead of enumerating addresses inline.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ipam_pool: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ipam_pool` reserves a block of IP address space under Azure Virtual Network Manager's own IP Address Management capability, that virtual networks draw non-overlapping address ranges from automatically.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_nat_gateway: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_nat_gateway` provides managed, scalable outbound internet connectivity (source NAT) for resources in an attached subnet, without requiring a public IP directly on each resource.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_int: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_interface` is the virtual network interface card attaching a VM to a subnet, carrying its own private (and optionally public) IP configuration.
`azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_interface_tap_configuration` mirrors a network interface's own traffic to a Virtual Network TAP destination for out-of-band monitoring or analysis.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_pro: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_profile` defines the network interface configuration used by container groups (e.g. Azure Container Instances) deployed directly into a virtual network subnet.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_sec: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_security_group` is a stateful firewall applied to a subnet or network interface, allowing or denying traffic based on its own ordered security rule(s).
azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_vir: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_virtual_appliance` deploys a third-party network virtual appliance (firewall, router) from the Azure Marketplace into a virtual hub, for traffic inspection and routing.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_dns: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_dns_zone_group` links a Private Endpoint to Private DNS zone(s), automatically creating and maintaining the DNS record(s) that resolve to the endpoint's private IP address.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_end: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_endpoint` is a network interface with a private IP address inside a virtual network, privately connecting to a specific Azure PaaS service or Private Link service without traversing the public internet.

`azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_endpoint_connection` represents one side of the connection between a Private Endpoint and the Private Link-enabled service it targets, tracking that connection's own approval state.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_lin: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_link_service` exposes a service behind a Standard Load Balancer for private consumption by other virtual networks via Private Endpoint, without requiring VNet peering.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_public_ipad: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_public_ipaddress` is a static or dynamic public IPv4 or IPv6 address that a load balancer, gateway, or VM can be assigned for internet-reachable connectivity.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_public_ippr: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_public_ipprefix` reserves a contiguous, statically allocated range of public IP addresses that individual public IP address resources can be created from.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_reachabilit: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_reachability_analysis_intent` defines the source and destination traffic path Azure Virtual Network Manager's own Network Verifier should evaluate for reachability, before any actual analysis run is executed.

`azure_network_virtualnetwork_reachability_analysis_run` is a single execution of Azure Virtual Network Manager's own Network Verifier against a reachability analysis intent, statically checking NSGs, routes, peering, and other configuration for whether the defined traffic path would actually succeed.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_route: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_route` is a single custom route within a route table, directing traffic matching an address prefix to a specific next hop.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_route_table: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_route_table` is a collection of custom route(s) that can be associated with subnet(s) to override their own default system routing.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_pa: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_partner_provider` integrates a supported third-party security provider (e.g. Check Point, Zscaler) with an Azure Firewall-managed virtual hub for traffic inspection.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_ru: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_rule` is a single custom allow/deny rule within a network security group, evaluated in priority order against matching traffic.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_static_cidr: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_static_cidr` tracks an IP address range already in use outside Azure Virtual Network Manager's own control (e.g. on-premises or manually allocated) within an IPAM pool, preventing it from being allocated again.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_subnet: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_subnet` is a range within a virtual network's own address space that resources (VMs, PaaS services) are deployed into, with its own NSG, route table, and delegation configuration.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_verifier_wo: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_verifier_workspace` is the top-level Azure Virtual Network Manager resource that reachability analysis intent(s) and their own analysis run(s) are created under.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_app: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_appliance_site` defines a branch site whose own address space is advertised to and routed through a network virtual appliance deployed in a virtual hub.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_net: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_network` is an Azure Virtual Network (VNet), the isolated network boundary that subnet(s), and the resources deployed into them, live within.

`azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_network_peering` connects two virtual networks together at the network layer, letting resources in each communicate using private IP addresses as if they were on the same network.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_rou: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_router` provisions Azure Route Server, a managed BGP route reflector that lets network virtual appliances exchange dynamic routes directly with a virtual network without static route table configuration.
`azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_router_peering` establishes a BGP peering session between Azure Route Server and a network virtual appliance's own router.
azure_network_virtualwan_bgp_connection: `azure_network_virtualwan_bgp_connection` establishes a BGP peering session between a Virtual WAN hub and an external router, exchanging dynamic routes without static route configuration.
azure_network_virtualwan_connection_poli: `azure_network_virtualwan_connection_policy` restricts which point-to-site VPN group(s) or attribute(s) are permitted to establish a connection through a Virtual WAN P2S gateway.
azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_c: `azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_connection` connects an ExpressRoute circuit to a Virtual WAN hub's own ExpressRoute gateway.
azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_g: `azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_gateway` provisions the ExpressRoute gateway within a Virtual WAN hub, that ExpressRoute circuit connection(s) terminate on.
azure_network_virtualwan_hub_ip_configur: `azure_network_virtualwan_hub_ip_configuration` defines the IP configuration for a Virtual WAN hub's own routing infrastructure, e.g. for Azure Firewall integration.
azure_network_virtualwan_hub_route_table: `azure_network_virtualwan_hub_route_table` is a route table within a Virtual WAN hub controlling which routes are propagated to and associated with specific connection(s).
azure_network_virtualwan_hub_virtual_net: `azure_network_virtualwan_hub_virtual_network_connection` connects a spoke virtual network to a Virtual WAN hub, integrating it into the hub's own any-to-any routing topology.
azure_network_virtualwan_network_virtual: `azure_network_virtualwan_network_virtual_appliance_connection` connects a network virtual appliance deployed in a Virtual WAN hub to the hub's own routing infrastructure.
azure_network_virtualwan_p2_svpn_gateway: `azure_network_virtualwan_p2_svpn_gateway` provisions the point-to-site VPN gateway within a Virtual WAN hub, that individual remote client(s) connect to.
azure_network_virtualwan_route_map: `azure_network_virtualwan_route_map` transforms route attributes (prefix, community, AS-path) as they're advertised to or received from a Virtual WAN hub connection, for advanced routing policy scenarios.
azure_network_virtualwan_routing_intent: `azure_network_virtualwan_routing_intent` configures a Virtual WAN hub to route all internet-bound or private inter-hub traffic through a security appliance (e.g. Azure Firewall) by default, without manual route table configuration.
azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub: `azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub` is the regional routing hub within a Virtual WAN, that spoke virtual network(s), VPN/ExpressRoute gateway(s), and security appliance(s) connect to.
azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub_rou: `azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub_route_table_v2` is the current-generation route table resource for a Virtual WAN hub, supporting more granular route propagation and association rules than the original hub route table.
azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_wan: `azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_wan` is the top-level Virtual WAN resource that virtual hub(s) across regions are created within, providing a unified, Microsoft-managed global network backbone.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_connection: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_connection` connects a remote VPN site to a Virtual WAN hub's own site-to-site VPN gateway.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway` provisions the site-to-site VPN gateway within a Virtual WAN hub, that VPN site connection(s) terminate on.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway_nat: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway_nat_rule` applies NAT translation to traffic passing through a Virtual WAN VPN gateway, for connecting sites with overlapping address spaces.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_server_conf: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_server_configuration` defines the authentication method and protocol(s) a Virtual WAN point-to-site VPN gateway accepts client connections with.

`azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_server_configuration_policy_group` groups point-to-site VPN client(s) by attribute (e.g. Entra ID group) and applies a distinct address pool or configuration to that group.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_site: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_site` represents a remote, on-premises site (its own address space and link details) that connects into a Virtual WAN hub via site-to-site VPN.
azure_proximity_placement_group: `azure_proximity_placement_group` pulls compute resources physically together in the same datacenter, the opposite goal of an availability set or zone, which deliberately spread VMs apart for resilience. It exists for workloads where network latency between tiers matters more than fault isolation -- a database tier and an application tier on different hardware types can still be pinned into the same proximity group. The group is a colocation constraint, not a capacity guarantee: it's pinned to a datacenter by whichever resource uses it first, and stays pinned until every resource in the group is stopped or deleted.
azure_restore_point: `azure_restore_point` is a point-in-time capture of every disk attached to one VM -- the OS disk and each data disk gets its own disk restore point inside it. The first restore point is a full copy; every one after that captures only the changes since the previous one, and individual disks can be excluded to control storage cost. Restoring a VM means restoring each disk from its own disk restore point, then reassembling them.
azure_restore_point_collection: `azure_restore_point_collection` is the real Azure Resource Manager resource a VM's own restore points live inside -- scoped to exactly one VM, it's what you create first before any individual restore point can exist.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_action_re: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_action_response` defines a playbook (Logic App) that an alert rule or automation rule triggers to run automatically in Microsoft Sentinel.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_alert_rul: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_alert_rule` defines the detection logic (a scheduled query, ML analytics, or fusion rule) Microsoft Sentinel evaluates to generate an alert from matching log or signal data.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_automatio: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_automation_rule` automatically applies action(s) (assign an owner, run a playbook, close as false-positive) to Microsoft Sentinel incident(s) matching a defined condition.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_bookmark: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_bookmark` saves a specific set of log query results in Microsoft Sentinel for later reference during an investigation.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_data_conn: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_data_connector` ingests log or event data from a specific source (an Azure service, a third-party product, or a custom feed) into Microsoft Sentinel.

`azure_securityinsights_openapi_data_connector_definition` defines the connection UI and configuration schema for a Microsoft Sentinel data connector, used when publishing a connector as reusable content.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_incident: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_incident` is a Microsoft Sentinel security incident, grouping related alert(s) together as the unit an analyst investigates and resolves.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_incident_: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_incident_comment` is a single comment posted on a Microsoft Sentinel incident during investigation.
`azure_securityinsights_openapi_incident_task` is a single checklist item tracked against a Microsoft Sentinel incident, part of a structured investigation or response playbook.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_metadata_: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_metadata_model` describes the source, author, and dependency metadata for a piece of Microsoft Sentinel content (an analytics rule, playbook, or workbook) published to the content hub.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_package_m: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_package_model` is an installable bundle of related Microsoft Sentinel content (analytics rules, workbooks, playbooks) for a specific solution, distributed through the content hub.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_relation: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_relation` links two Microsoft Sentinel entities (e.g. an incident to a bookmark) together as a tracked relationship.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_security_: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_security_mlanalytics_setting` configures a Microsoft Sentinel built-in machine learning analytics detection (e.g. anomalous sign-in detection).
azure_securityinsights_openapi_sentinel_: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_sentinel_onboarding_state` tracks whether Microsoft Sentinel has been onboarded (activated) onto a specific Log Analytics workspace.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_source_co: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_source_control` links a Microsoft Sentinel workspace to an external Git repository, syncing analytics rule and other content definitions from source control.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_template_: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_template_model` is a reusable content template (e.g. for an analytics rule) published to the Microsoft Sentinel content hub, that new instances can be created from.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_threat_in: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_threat_intelligence_information` is a single threat intelligence indicator (an IP, domain, or hash) ingested into Microsoft Sentinel, used to enrich and match against incoming log data.
azure_securityinsights_openapi_watchlist: `azure_securityinsights_openapi_watchlist` is a named, uploaded reference dataset (e.g. a list of high-value assets) in Microsoft Sentinel, joinable against log query results for enrichment and filtering.
`azure_securityinsights_openapi_watchlist_item` is a single row of data within a Microsoft Sentinel watchlist.
azure_ssh_public_key_resource: `azure_ssh_public_key_resource` stores an SSH public key in Azure as its own standalone resource, independent of any single VM. Once created (generated fresh as RSA or Ed25519, or uploaded from an existing key you already have), the same stored key can be attached to any number of new VM deployments instead of pasting the raw key text in every time.
azure_virtual_machine: `azure_virtual_machine` is Azure's own core compute resource -- real, on-demand virtualized hardware you configure yourself (size, OS, disks, networking) rather than a managed platform service. It's the choice when a workload needs more control over its own environment than Azure's PaaS options offer, at the cost of still having to patch, configure, and maintain it yourself.
azure_virtual_machine_diagnostic_run_com: `azure_virtual_machine_diagnostic_run_command` runs a script against one specific VM instance inside a scale set through the VM agent, the same real Run Command mechanism Azure uses for general VM management -- diagnosing and remediating an instance's access or network problems without needing direct remote access to it.
azure_virtual_machine_extension: `azure_virtual_machine_extension` installs a small, publisher-provided application onto a running VM after deployment -- monitoring agents, security tooling, and custom scripts are all shipped this way. Extensions are managed entirely through the Azure platform, never by logging into the VM directly, and their own lifecycle (install, upgrade, remove) is tracked outside the guest OS.
azure_virtual_machine_run_command: `azure_virtual_machine_run_command` runs a script inside a VM through the VM agent for general machine or application management -- fetching content, changing configuration, or one-off diagnostics. This is Azure's original, action-oriented Run Command shape: one script, one active execution, a 90-minute limit. Azure's newer Managed Run Command variant exists separately for recurring or multi-script scenarios this shape isn't built for.
azure_virtual_machine_scale_set: `azure_virtual_machine_scale_set` manages a group of load-balanced VM instances as a single resource, built from one common base image and configuration. The set can automatically grow or shrink in response to real demand or a defined schedule, and spreading instances across fault domains or availability zones protects the application from a single instance's failure -- up to 1,000 instances for gallery or custom images, 600 for a managed image.
azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_extensio: `azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_extension` applies the same real VM extension mechanism (post-deployment configuration and automation) to every instance in a scale set at once, defined a single time at the scale-set level instead of being installed on each VM instance individually.
azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_vm: `azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_vm` represents one individual VM instance that's part of a scale set, letting that specific instance be read or managed on its own rather than only through the scale set as a whole.
azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_vmextens: `azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_vmextension` installs a VM extension on one specific instance within a scale set, rather than on every instance the way the scale-set-level extension resource does -- the per-instance counterpart for cases that don't need a uniform, set-wide rollout.
azure_vmware_vmware_addon: `azure_vmware_vmware_addon` enables an optional integration (e.g. HCX, Site Recovery, or Arc) on an Azure VMware Solution private cloud.
azure_vmware_vmware_cloud_link: `azure_vmware_vmware_cloud_link` connects two Azure VMware Solution private clouds together for cross-private-cloud VM migration and networking.
azure_vmware_vmware_cluster: `azure_vmware_vmware_cluster` is a cluster of node(s) within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud, the unit VMware ESXi/vSAN compute and storage capacity is added in.
azure_vmware_vmware_datastore: `azure_vmware_vmware_datastore` attaches external storage (e.g. Azure NetApp Files, Pure Storage Cloud) as a datastore to an Azure VMware Solution cluster, supplementing its own native vSAN capacity.
azure_vmware_vmware_express_route_author: `azure_vmware_vmware_express_route_authorization` generates an authorization key letting an external ExpressRoute circuit connect to an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own ExpressRoute circuit.
azure_vmware_vmware_global_reach_connect: `azure_vmware_vmware_global_reach_connection` peers an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own ExpressRoute circuit with another ExpressRoute circuit, extending connectivity to on-premises or another Azure VNet.
azure_vmware_vmware_hcx_enterprise_site: `azure_vmware_vmware_hcx_enterprise_site` activates a VMware HCX site connecting an on-premises VMware environment to an Azure VMware Solution private cloud, for live workload migration.
azure_vmware_vmware_license: `azure_vmware_vmware_license` reports the VMware software license key(s) associated with an Azure VMware Solution private cloud.
azure_vmware_vmware_maintenance: `azure_vmware_vmware_maintenance` reports scheduled maintenance event(s) affecting an Azure VMware Solution private cloud.
azure_vmware_vmware_placement_policy: `azure_vmware_vmware_placement_policy` constrains which host(s) or VM(s) can run together (or must run apart) within an Azure VMware Solution cluster, for licensing or availability requirements.
azure_vmware_vmware_private_cloud: `azure_vmware_vmware_private_cloud` is the top-level Azure VMware Solution resource -- a dedicated, VMware-based private cloud environment (vCenter, NSX-T, vSAN) running on Azure infrastructure.
azure_vmware_vmware_pure_storage_policy: `azure_vmware_vmware_pure_storage_policy` defines the vVols storage policy applied to VM(s) using Pure Storage Cloud as a datastore within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud.
azure_vmware_vmware_script_execution: `azure_vmware_vmware_script_execution` runs a predefined PowerShell script package against an Azure VMware Solution private cloud, for administrative operations the vCenter UI doesn't directly expose.
azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_dhc: `azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_dhcp` configures a DHCP server or relay for VM workload network(s) within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own NSX-T environment.
azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_dns: `azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_dns_service` configures a DNS forwarding service for VM workload network(s) within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own NSX-T environment.
`azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_dns_zone` defines a DNS zone resolved by an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own workload network DNS service.
azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_por: `azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_port_mirroring` mirrors traffic from one workload network segment to another within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own NSX-T environment, for monitoring.
azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_pub: `azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_public_ip` assigns a public IP address reachable by VM workload(s) within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own NSX-T environment.
azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_seg: `azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_segment` is a logical Layer 2 network segment within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own NSX-T environment, that workload VM(s) are attached to.
azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_vmg: `azure_vmware_vmware_workload_network_vmgroup` groups VM(s) together within an Azure VMware Solution private cloud's own NSX-T environment, for applying network security or DFW rule(s) collectively.
azure_web_openapi_ai_gateway: `azure_web_openapi_ai_gateway` configures the AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management (public preview, 2026), a dedicated gateway for AI traffic that fronts model and MCP server endpoints behind one governed entry point with policies like semantic caching and token rate limiting.
azure_web_openapi_app_service_environmen: `azure_web_openapi_app_service_environment_resource` provisions an App Service Environment, a single-tenant, isolated deployment of App Service running inside the caller's own virtual network.
azure_web_openapi_app_service_plan: `azure_web_openapi_app_service_plan` defines the compute tier and capacity (VM size, instance count) that one or more App Service web apps run on.
azure_web_openapi_backup_item: `azure_web_openapi_backup_item` is a single completed or scheduled backup of an App Service web app's own content and configuration.
azure_web_openapi_certificate: `azure_web_openapi_certificate` is a TLS certificate uploaded to App Service, bindable to a custom domain on a web app.
azure_web_openapi_database_connection: `azure_web_openapi_database_connection` links an App Service web app to a database resource, storing the connection string used to reach it.
azure_web_openapi_default_error_response: `azure_web_openapi_default_error_response` is App Service's own standard API error envelope, returned when a request to the App Service management API fails -- not a deployable resource in its own right.
azure_web_openapi_deployment: `azure_web_openapi_deployment` is a single deployment record for an App Service web app, tracking a specific push of code to the app.
azure_web_openapi_function_envelope: `azure_web_openapi_function_envelope` describes a single function within an Azure Functions app hosted on App Service infrastructure, including its own trigger, bindings, and configuration.
azure_web_openapi_host_name_binding: `azure_web_openapi_host_name_binding` maps a custom domain hostname to an App Service web app, routing that hostname's own traffic to it.
azure_web_openapi_hybrid_connection: `azure_web_openapi_hybrid_connection` establishes outbound-only connectivity from an App Service web app to an on-premises or other-network TCP endpoint, without requiring inbound firewall changes.
azure_web_openapi_identifier: `azure_web_openapi_identifier` verifies ownership of a custom domain for use with an App Service web app, via a domain verification identifier record.
azure_web_openapi_kube_environment: `azure_web_openapi_kube_environment` is the legacy App Service Kubernetes Environment resource, an earlier Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes hosting environment for App Service and Functions, since superseded by newer Container Apps-based hosting.
azure_web_openapi_premier_add_on: `azure_web_openapi_premier_add_on` attaches a premium App Service marketplace add-on (e.g. an APM integration) to a web app.
azure_web_openapi_public_certificate: `azure_web_openapi_public_certificate` uploads a public certificate (no private key) to an App Service web app, made available to the app's own code for validating outbound connections.
azure_web_openapi_relay_service_connecti: `azure_web_openapi_relay_service_connection_entity` configures an App Service web app's own Azure Relay-based hybrid connection endpoint details.
azure_web_openapi_remote_private_endpoin: `azure_web_openapi_remote_private_endpoint_connection_armresource` represents a Private Endpoint connection to an App Service resource, tracking its own approval state.
azure_web_openapi_site: `azure_web_openapi_site` is an App Service web app (or Function App), the deployable application resource that App Service Plan compute serves.
azure_web_openapi_site_config_resource: `azure_web_openapi_site_config_resource` holds the detailed runtime configuration (stack, always-on, app settings behavior) for an App Service web app.
azure_web_openapi_site_container: `azure_web_openapi_site_container` defines a single container image and its own configuration for a multi-container App Service web app.
azure_web_openapi_site_extension_info: `azure_web_openapi_site_extension_info` is a site extension (e.g. a diagnostics or monitoring add-on) installed on an App Service web app.
azure_web_openapi_source_control: `azure_web_openapi_source_control` configures continuous deployment for an App Service web app from a linked source control repository.
azure_web_openapi_static_site_armresourc: `azure_web_openapi_static_site_armresource` provisions an Azure Static Web App, a globally distributed static site with an integrated serverless API backend built from a linked Git repository.
azure_web_openapi_static_site_basic_auth: `azure_web_openapi_static_site_basic_auth_properties_armresource` configures basic HTTP authentication protecting a Static Web App's own environment(s).
azure_web_openapi_static_site_custom_dom: `azure_web_openapi_static_site_custom_domain_overview_armresource` maps a custom domain to a Static Web App.
azure_web_openapi_static_site_linked_bac: `azure_web_openapi_static_site_linked_backend_armresource` links an external API backend (e.g. an App Service or Container App) to a Static Web App, exposed through its own integrated `/api` routing.
azure_web_openapi_static_site_user_provi: `azure_web_openapi_static_site_user_provided_function_app_armresource` links an existing, caller-managed Azure Functions app as the API backend for a Static Web App.
azure_web_openapi_vnet_gateway: `azure_web_openapi_vnet_gateway` represents the App Service-side gateway endpoint of a virtual network integration connection.
azure_web_openapi_vnet_info_resource: `azure_web_openapi_vnet_info_resource` describes the virtual network an App Service web app is integrated with, letting the app reach resources inside it.
azure_web_openapi_worker_pool_resource: `azure_web_openapi_worker_pool_resource` defines a named pool of worker compute within an App Service Environment, that web app(s) can be scaled onto independently of the environment's own front-end capacity.
azure_web_openapi_workflow_envelope: `azure_web_openapi_workflow_envelope` describes a single Logic Apps (Standard) workflow hosted within an App Service-based Logic App resource, including its own definition and run history metadata.
